newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil mulling credit restrictions -- newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil mulling credit restrictions -- newspaper.

text.p: The Brazilian government may approve new credit restrictions at a National Monetary Council meeting in late April to slow consumption growth, especially of automobiles and electrical goods, a local newspaper said.
O Estado de Sao Paulo, quoting unnamed Finance Ministry officials, said the move also would help ease Brazil's swelling trade deficit because cars and electrical goods contain many imported parts.
Estado also quoted Finance Ministry Political Secretary Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros as saying the government wants "to reduce the rate of growth in consumption."
"We don't want to reduce consumption, we don't want recession. But we can't sustain consumption growth of up to 50 percent with a 70 percent rise in credit, as is occurring," he said.
Ministry Executive Secretary Pedro Parente and Central Bank International Affairs chief Gustavo Franco, meanwhile, also said the government is mindful of the growth in consumption, Estado said.
The paper said bank credit to individuals grew by 70 percent in January compared to January 1996.
